This matter is taken up through Hybrid Arrangement (Virtual /Physical Mode).
2.
Heard learned counsel appearing for the Petitioner and learned Additional Standing Counsel appearing for the State- Opposite Party.
Perused the materials placed before this Court.

3. The present bail application under Section 483 of B.N.S.S. has been filed by the Petitioner for regular bail in connection with Cyber Crime P.S.Case No.16 of 2022 corresponding to G.R.Case No.1531 of 2022, pending in the Court of learned J.M.F.C. (Cog.-III), Cuttack for alleged commission of offence punishable under Sections 120-B, 419, 420 467, 468, 471/34 of the Indian Penal Code read with Section 66(C)/66(D) of I.T.Act.
4.
Learned counsel for the Petitioner submits that earlier this matter was not before any other Bench of this Court .
It is submitted by the learned counsel for the Petitioner that the Petitioner, who is a lady having two children, is languishing in custody since 22.04.2024.
Learned counsel for the Petitioner further contended that as per the F.I.R. allegation out of Rs.28,00,000/-, a sum of Rs.11,55,000/- was transferred to the bank account of the present Petitioner.
He further contended that the Petitioner lives in the State of Assam.
Learned counsel for the Petitioner further submitted that the Petitioner is an innocent lady and is not aware of transfer of such huge amount to her account.
He further submitted that the Petitioner has been falsely implicated in the present case.

1 further contended that the Petitioner does not have any criminal antecedent and that she is ready and willing to abide by any terms and conditions in the event of her release on bail.

5. Learned Additional Standing Counsel on the other hand submitted that the principal accused and the perpetrator of the present cyber crime is a Nigerian citizen who was talking to the victim constantly and money was transferred on the request of the principal accused.
He further contended that on enquiry, Cyber Police has found out that the account was opened in the name of the Petitioner.
However, the amount was delivered somewhere in Rajasthan and the money was withdrawn from an ATM at Delhi.

On a subsequent query from this Court learned counsel for the Petitioner submitted that as per the investigation the money was withdrawn from the ATM at Delhi by the principal accused Nizarian citizen.
He further submitted that the principal accused i.e., the Nigerian is in custody.
On such ground, learned counsel for the State submitted that since the account of the Petitioner has been used in the present crime, she is not entitled to be released on bail at this juncture.

6. On a careful examination of the materials on record and taking into consideration the submissions of the learned counsels for the parties, this Court observes that the present case involves an instance of a cyber crime.

The preliminary investigation conducted so far by the Cyber Police reveals that although the account of the Petitioner was used in the crime, however, the principal accused was in Delhi and it appears that the account of the Petitioner has been misused by the principal accused and that there are ample materials on record to establish the fact that alleged sum of money has been withdrawn by the principal accused from an ATM at Delhi.

Taking into consideration the surrounding facts and circumstances as well as the materials so far collected and keeping in view the period of custodial detention of the Petitioner and the fact that the Petitioner does not have any criminal antecedent, this Court is inclined to release the Petitioner on bail subject to imposition of stringent conditions.

7. Hence, it is directed that the Petitioner be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing bail bond of Rs.40,000/- (Rupees Forty thousand) with one local solvent surety for the like amount to the satisfaction of the Court in seisin over the matter.
Release of the Petitioner shall be subject to such terms and conditions that would be deemed as just and proper.

While imposing conditions,
learned court in seisin over the matter shall impose a condition whereby the Petitioner shall appear before the concerned P.S., under whose jurisdiction the Petitioner is residing in the State of Assam,
once in a fortnight preferably on Sunday between 10 A.M. to 1 P.M. till conclusion of trial.
Violation of any of the conditions shall entail cancellation of bail.
8. It is further directed that the bail granted to the Petitioner be subject to the condition that the court below shall verify the criminal antecedent of the Petitioner.
In the event the it is found that Petitioner is having any similar criminal antecedent, this bail order shall automatically stand revoked.
9. The BLAPL is, accordingly, disposed of.
( A.K. Mohapatra) Judge RKS Location: High Court of Orissa Rashida Khatun vs State Of Odisha .....
